title: Midas Touch: Invalid-Data Assisted Reliability and Performance Boost for 3d High-Density Flash
problem: 3D QLC NAND flash requires two-step programming in a specific sequence, causing data to become invalid between steps. The second-step programming operates on partially-invalid wordlines, creating reliability and performance challenges.
motivation: High-density 3D NAND flash like QLC is increasingly prevalent for data-intensive applications, making improvements to their reliability and performance critical.
method: The approach addresses invalid data created during 3D QLC's two-step programming process with three strategies. First, a fast re-programming scheme rewrites valid data surviving the first step more quickly, reducing latency. Second, a high-reliability scheme safely programs the partially-invalid wordlines in the second step without data loss. Third, an adaptive allocation strategy dynamically routes data between single-level (SLC) and quad-level (QLC) storage regions, avoiding situations where invalid programming would occur.
key_novelty: Instead of treating invalid programming as a limitation to avoid, the work uses it as an opportunity to boost both performance and reliability of valid data in 3D QLC flash.
contributions: High-efficiency re-programming (RP) scheme achieving 13.51% programming time reduction
High-reliability not-programming (NP) scheme reducing bit error rate by 32.8%
Adaptive data allocation (ADA) strategy for dynamic SLC/QLC region management
Combined approach delivering 30% lifetime extension and 4.8% energy reduction

metrics.other: 32.8% BER reduction, 30% lifetime extension, 12% refreshing overhead reduction, 4.8% energy reduction

limitations: Limitations are not explicitly discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Flash memory reliability and performance optimization
